title: Observer: tell everyone who's listening
summary: Keep a list of listeners and call each one when something changes, so the thing that changes doesn't need to know who cares.

say.never: When you subscribe to a channel, the channel doesn't know you personally. It keeps a list of subscribers, and when a new video goes up, it tells everyone on the list. That's the **Observer** pattern. The thing being watched keeps a `List` of **listeners**. Anyone can add themselves. When something changes, it calls a method on every listener in the list.
say.bit: **Observer**: keep a `List` of listeners; on a change, call each one.

say.never: A sensor is read about 50 times a second. If it told its listeners on every read, the LEDs would hear "you have a piece" 50 times a second. So remember the last value, and only tell the listeners when the new reading is *different*. Update the remembered value before you tell anyone, so a listener that asks "what's the value now?" gets the new answer.
say.bit: Tell listeners only when the value changes, and save the new value before telling them.

steps.title: In your lesson: Only when it changes

say.never: `BeamBreak` is the thing being watched, and `PieceListener` is the listener's interface. `addListener` and `removeListener` change `listeners_`. `update(beam_blocked)` compares the reading with `has_piece_`. If they're the same, do nothing. If not, save the new value in `has_piece_`, then loop over `listeners_` and call `onChange(has_piece_)` on each.
say.bit: `addListener`/`removeListener` edit `listeners_`. `update`: on a change, save `has_piece_`, then `onChange` each listener.
